title: 1. The front door: what a repository opens on

sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: A person opening a repository should meet its purpose and a way in, not a data dump.

sections.name: body
sections.label: The evidence
sections.content: The owner, 2026-10-26: "A srs repository should have a structure that makes sense to browse" (29d4cbd4). The affirmed problems are SP-119 (a repository opened for the first time reads as a data dump) and SP-48 (every repository opens as the same engine view). The generic editor is many people's first experience of SRS (18d1c388), and a repository should identify itself to a cold agent (a693b256). Decided: the root container is required and its identity record is the repository's purpose (RFC-013). Not decided: what the front door is; RFC-013's root view binding (OQ-1) was never specified, and srs-web simply opens the first composition. LiveWyer Insight puts a reading guide in the identity record and installs its front-door document first (finding 6439b0db).

sections.name: principle
sections.label: Principle
sections.content: The identity record is the front matter and reading guide; one document is the front door. Decided in part (RFC-013), practised (LiveWyer, srs-context), the front door undecided.
